tools.name: approve_plan
tools.title: Approve plan
tools.description: Record that another agent or subagent reviewed the plan of an issue. Use it in a project with approvalMode agent_review, before you set in_progress. The reviewer reads the plan of planRevision; reviewer is its name and reviewNote its findings. The author of a plan does not review it. Fails with invalid_input in approvalMode user, for an issue without a plan, and for a planRevision that is not the newest: then call get_issue and review the newest plan. A plan with new text clears the approval.

planRevision.description: planRevision of the issue, as the reviewer read it

reviewer.description: Name of the agent or subagent that reviewed the plan

reviewNote.description: Markdown: the findings of the reviewer, at least 20 characters

tools.name: claim_request
tools.title: Claim request
tools.description: Claim an open or reopened request before you edit code for it. Status becomes in_progress. Claiming a request that you already hold succeeds and changes nothing. Fails with invalid_transition when the status does not allow it or another agent holds it: then take the next request.

tools.name: comment_on_issue
tools.title: Comment on issue
tools.description: Add a Markdown comment to the thread of an issue, in any status. A step of the work on a tracked issue is a comment, not a new issue. With awaiting_user_input, name in a comment what the user must decide. Write technical English, as short as possible, and only what a later reader needs.

tools.name: create_issue
tools.title: Create issue
tools.description: Create an issue of a project. Its key is the project key, a hyphen, and the next number of the project, for example SM-12. Look through the open issues of the project first, and continue one that covers the request. status is draft while the problem is incomplete, and backlog or todo when it is ready; backlog and todo need problem. Write technical English, as short as possible, and only what a later reader needs.

project.description: Project key from list_projects, for example SM

title.description: One line that names the issue

problem.description: Markdown: what the user wants, and how to tell that it is done

tools.name: get_issue
tools.title: Get issue
tools.description: Read one issue in full: the four sections, planRevision, the plan approval, allowedStatuses, its links, and its thread. A section_changed entry of the thread names its section and holds no text.

tools.name: get_request
tools.title: Get request
tools.description: Return one request in full: title, body, thread, anchor with a code snapshot at the review commit, linked commits, location, how to deliver the work (delivery), and the actions you may take now (allowedActions). `at` locates the anchor at another commit that the server's clone has (pushed, or committed in a local repository); by default the location is at the default-branch head. Your working tree can differ: find the code with anchor.snapshot, its before and after lines, and anchor.symbol.fqn. A general request has anchor, location, and excerpt null. It belongs to the whole review, and its body and thread say what to change. A request with title null has no title: give it one with set_request_title before you claim it. type says what the user asks for: change, a code change; question, claim it, answer with reply_to_request, change no code, then mark_ready_for_review with a note that points to the answer; rule, claim it, add the rule as one bullet in the user's words under `## Rules from Slopmower` in AGENTS.md at the repository root (create the file when it is missing), add `@AGENTS.md` to CLAUDE.md when it exists and does not import AGENTS.md, fix the anchored code when it breaks the rule, all in one commit, then link, mark ready, and follow the rule from then on. group, when not null, makes the request one unit of feedback with the other requests of that group: read them with list_requests and group, and handle them together in one commit.

at.description: Commit SHA (7-64 hex digits) to locate the anchor at

context.description: Lines of context around the located code to include as excerpt

tools.name: get_updates
tools.title: Get updates
tools.description: Return what changed in one review since `cursor`, grouped by request, leaving out your own actions. Without a cursor, return every request that waits for you with its unseen events. Always keep the returned cursor for the next call; if hasMore is true, call again at once. reviewState 'closed' means stop.

cursor.description: The cursor from the previous call. Null returns everything that waits for you.

limit.description: Maximum events (with a cursor) or requests (without one)

tools.name: link_commits
tools.title: Link commits
tools.description: Record that a commit implements one or more requests that you hold (status in_progress). Use the full SHA from `git rev-parse HEAD`. The commit may be unpushed: the link stays pending until the server's clone has it. Linking does not finish a request.

requestIds.description: Every request that this commit covers, all from one review

note.description: Optional note shown with the link

tools.name: link_issues
tools.title: Link issues
tools.description: Link two issues, with the reason in note. A link has no direction: both issues show it. Link a follow-up issue to its origin. A link of an issue to itself, and a second link of the same two issues, fail with invalid_input.

note.description: Markdown: the reason for the link

tools.name: link_pull_request
tools.title: Link pull request
tools.description: Record that a pull request implements one or more requests: each one in_progress and held by you, or ready_for_review. For a GitHub repository the URL is https://github.com/{owner}/{name}/pull/{number} of the reviewed repository. A local repository has no pull requests. Linking does not change the status. Open a pull request when delivery.pullRequest of get_request is true; when it is null, only when the user or the repository's instructions ask for it.

requestIds.description: Every request that this pull request covers, all from one review

note.description: Optional note shown with the link

tools.name: list_issues
tools.title: List issues
tools.description: List the issues of one project as summaries, newest updatedAt first. Call get_issue for the sections, the links, and the thread.

project.description: Project key from list_projects, for example SM

tools.name: list_projects
tools.title: List projects
tools.description: List the projects of the issue tracker that this token sees, with key, name, approvalMode, and the names of their repositories. Track the work on a repository as issues of the project that lists it. A token of one repository sees only the project of that repository.

tools.name: list_repositories
tools.title: List repositories
tools.description: List the repositories that this token can see: id, source (github or local), name, default branch, and number of open reviews. Use the name or id as `repository` in list_reviews.

tools.name: list_requests
tools.title: List requests
tools.description: List the change requests of one review, oldest first, with optional filters. Returns summaries: title is null while a request has none, and summary is the title or else the first line of the body as plain text. Call get_request for the body, thread, anchor, and location. Requests with the same group are one unit of feedback: pass group to read them all, claim each, make one change in one commit, link it to every request of the group, and mark each ready with the same note; with requireApproval, propose the same plan on each.

awaiting.description: Only requests where it is this party's turn; "agent" means you

path.description: Only requests whose file path starts with this prefix; general requests never match

outdated.description: Only requests whose code changed (true) or did not change (false) on the default branch

suggestion.description: Only suggestions in this state; requests that the user opened never match

group.description: Only requests of this group, an exact match; requests without a group never match

tools.name: list_reviews
tools.title: List reviews
tools.description: List the reviews of one repository, newest first. Only open reviews unless includeClosed is true. Each review is pinned to one commit and holds its own requests; pass its id as `review` to get_updates and list_requests.

repository.description: Repository ID, GitHub owner/name, or local directory name

tools.name: mark_ready_for_review
tools.title: Mark ready for review
tools.description: Tell the user that a request you hold is done. The note says what you changed and how you tested it. Every linked commit must be in the server's clone: for GitHub repositories push first (the server fetches once), otherwise this fails with commits_not_available. A request that needs no code change may have no commits; say why in the note.

note.description: What you changed and how you tested it

tools.name: mark_wont_do
tools.title: Mark won't do
tools.description: Decline an open or reopened request, or one that you hold. Give evidence that the user can check: a file and line, a test result, a conflicting requirement, or why the request is wrong. At least 20 characters. The user then verifies or reopens it.

tools.name: propose_solution
tools.title: Propose solution
tools.description: Propose how you will solve a request that you hold, before you link commits. Required when the request has requireApproval true; also useful when the request is unclear or large. A new proposal replaces the current one. The user approves it or requests changes: the decision comes back through get_updates, and get_request shows it in proposal.state. Until the user approves, link_commits and mark_ready_for_review fail with invalid_transition.

plan.description: Markdown plan: what you will change, and why

diff.description: Optional unified diff of the change from `git diff`, at most 9 files

tools.name: release_request
tools.title: Release request
tools.description: Give back a request that you claimed but will not finish. Its status returns to what it was before the claim (open or reopened).

note.description: Why you stop, for the user

tools.name: reply_to_request
tools.title: Reply to request
tools.description: Add a comment to a request's thread, in any status. Set question to true when you need the user's answer; the request then waits for the user and comes back through get_updates when they reply. Put each question you need answered in questions: the user answers each with Yes, No, or text, and the answers come back as a user comment whose questions hold each question with its answer.

question.description: True when you need an answer from the user

questions.description: Questions for the user, each answered with Yes, No, or text. A comment with questions is a question.

detail.description: Optional Markdown context of the question

tools.name: set_issue_status
tools.title: Set issue status
tools.description: Move an issue to another status. The server checks the state that the move gives: backlog, todo, in_progress, in_review, and done need problem; in_progress, in_review, and done need a plan that is approved as approvalMode says; in_review and done need result; wont_do needs note. done and wont_do from an agent: refused in approvalMode user, with reviewer and note in agent_review, free in self. todo to in_progress is the claim. A refusal is invalid_input on the field that breaks the rule. allowedStatuses of the issue lists what you can set now.

note.description: Markdown: why, for the thread. Required for wont_do, and for done in approvalMode agent_review

reviewer.description: Name of the agent or subagent that reviewed the result. Required for done and wont_do in approvalMode agent_review

tools.name: set_request_title
tools.title: Set request title
tools.description: Set the title of a request whose title is null: one line of at most 80 characters that summarizes its body. Call it before you claim such a request. Fails with invalid_transition when the request has a title; only the user changes a title.

title.description: One line of at most 80 characters that summarizes the body

tools.name: start_review
tools.title: Start review
tools.description: Start a review of one repository, pinned to one commit, when the user asks you to review code and no review was named. Without ref, the review pins the head of the default branch. Read the code at the returned commitSha, then call suggest_request once per finding.

repository.description: Repository ID, GitHub owner/name, or local directory name

ref.description: Branch, tag, or commit SHA to pin; null for the default branch

tools.name: suggest_request
tools.title: Suggest request
tools.description: Suggest one change while you review code. The suggestion is a request that waits for the user, who accepts or dismisses it; do not edit code for it. Give it a title: one line of at most 80 characters that summarizes the body. Use the narrowest anchor: anchorKind line or range with path, startLine, and endLine; symbol with path and the fully qualified name in symbol, for example App\Billing\InvoiceTotals::total(); file with path. Without anchorKind the suggestion concerns the whole review. If the server does not find the symbol, use a range. An accepted suggestion comes back through get_updates as a request that waits for you.

review.description: Review ID from start_review or list_reviews

title.description: One line of at most 80 characters that summarizes the body

body.description: Markdown: what to change, and why

anchorKind.description: line, range, symbol, or file; null for a general request

path.description: File path at the review commit; required with anchorKind

startLine.description: First line, for line and range

endLine.description: Last line, for line and range; equal to startLine for line

symbol.description: Fully qualified name of the symbol, for symbol

tools.name: unlink_commit
tools.title: Unlink commit
tools.description: Remove a commit link that you made by mistake from a request that you hold.

tools.name: unlink_pull_request
tools.title: Unlink pull request
tools.description: Remove a pull request link that you made by mistake from a request: in_progress and held by you, or ready_for_review.

tools.name: update_issue
tools.title: Update issue
tools.description: Change the title or the sections of an issue. Null leaves a field as it is; give at least one field. A section is Markdown. problem: what the user wants, and how to tell that it is done. plan: the steps, the files, and the tests. result: what was done, with the commit SHAs, and each deviation from the plan. followUps: what came up and was left out. A plan with new text clears its approval. An agent cannot change plan in in_progress or in_review, and no field of an issue in done or wont_do. Write technical English, as short as possible, and only what a later reader needs.

title.description: One line that names the issue

problem.description: Markdown: what the user wants, and how to tell that it is done

plan.description: Markdown: the steps, the files, and the tests

result.description: Markdown: what was done, with the commit SHAs, and each deviation from the plan

followUps.description: Markdown: what came up and was left out
